headline: GOLD LEAPS $40 ON U.S.-IRAN CEASEFIRE — OIL CRASHES 6%, Silver Rallies 1.9% as Monday Geopolitical Shock Reverses Inflation Trade
snippet: Gold surged approximately $40 to $4,110 per ounce and silver gained 1.9% to $59.27 on Monday after Washington and Tehran suspended hostilities, sending crude oil down more than 6% and collapsing the inflation-risk premium that had capped precious metals momentum into the Federal Reserve decision Wednesday. The dollar index fell 0.2%, lowering the cost of dollar-denominated gold for international buyers and amplifying the precious metals rally ahead of a Fed meeting that market pricing puts at roughly a 92% probability of a hold.

headline: PANORO'S SECOND DRILL NOW TURNING AT COTABAMBAS — Step-Out Holes Chase South Pit Extension at Peru's 1B-Tonne Cu-Au-Ag District (TSXV: PML)
snippet: Panoro Minerals (TSXV: PML) reported July 27 that a second drill rig has arrived and commenced step-out drilling at the South Pit of its 100%-owned Cotabambas Copper, Gold and Silver Project in Peru, a 1-billion-tonne resource holding 12.5 billion pounds copper equivalent. Metallurgical consultants are mobilizing to Cusco by end of July to begin representative core sampling as part of the expanded 45,000-metre campaign — launched after Phase 1 returned 317.6 metres of 1.04% CuEq — with up to five drill rigs expected on site by end of Q3 2026.

headline: GT RESOURCES WINS 10-YEAR CLASS III PERMIT AT CANALASK — Trail-Build Rights Unlock New Drill Access at Yukon Ni-Cu-Co-Pd Project (TSXV: GT)
snippet: GT Resources Inc. (TSXV: GT) received a 10-year Class III Exploration Permit for its Canalask Copper-Nickel Project in Yukon on July 27, a material upgrade over its prior authorization that critically allows construction of new trails providing access for additional drill targets. Best historical hole at Canalask: 1.95% nickel, 0.05% copper, 0.03% cobalt, 0.19 g/t gold, and 0.44 g/t palladium over 33.5 metres near surface — a polymetallic suite of elevated strategic interest given palladium supply concentration in Russia.

headline: HOMELAND URANIUM FULLY PERMITTED FOR 30-HOLE Cross Bones Inaugural Drill — Phase I Twins 1977 Colorado Discovery Holes; Fall 2026 Start (TSXV: HLU)
snippet: Homeland Uranium Corp. (TSXV: HLU) announced July 27 it has received all federal and state approvals — from the US Bureau of Land Management and Colorado's Division of Reclamation, Mining and Safety — for up to 30 diamond drill holes at its 100%-owned Cross Bones Uranium Project in Moffat and Rio Blanco Counties. Phase I will consist of 4-6 holes twinning Anschutz Uranium Corp.'s 1977-78 discovery holes, with drilling targeted to commence fall 2026 and permits valid through June 2028.

headline: DINERO VENTURES CONFIRMS Kolbe REE Zone — 829.6m in 7 Holes Identifies Parallel Rare Earth Dykes at Mt Bisson Magnetic Anomaly, BC (TSXV: DNO)
snippet: Dinero Ventures Ltd. (TSXV: DNO) completed Phase I drilling at its 100%-owned Mt Bisson REE Property — 65 km northwest of Mackenzie, BC — on July 27, with all 7 holes from 2 pads (829.6 metres total) encountering rare earth-bearing mineralisation confirming parallel REE-bearing dyke zones along the western margin of a 3 km × 9 km magnetic anomaly. Six REE-mineralised localities have been identified at Mt Bisson, with Kolbe and Central zones returning the highest values to date; Phase I assays are pending.

headline: DYSPROSIUM $2,250/KG AND CLIMBING — Oregon Group: All 18 Rare Earth Elements Rose in July, Average +16.7%, as China's Export Grip Tightens Further
snippet: The Oregon Group's critical minerals team reports all 18 rare earth elements tracked rose in price in July 2026 — averaging +16.7% — led by germanium (+27.8%), dysprosium (+25.4% to approximately $2,250/kg, up eightfold from April 2025), and terbium, as China's successive rounds of export control tightening create domestic-to-international price gaps of up to 100 times. Western manufacturers continue to report inability to source commercial volumes of heavy rare earth oxides, metals, or alloys with reliable delivery, suggesting the pricing dislocation is structural rather than speculative.
